resources.purpose: Base of the Sterling Theia workbench image (node:24 bookworm-slim, build and runtime stages; the release image published to GHCR), and build stage of the relay and hub images.
resources.licence: MIT (Node.js); Debian packages under their own licences
resources.evidence: Pinned by sha256 digest in every Dockerfile; the Release workflow smoke-tests the workbench image and records its GHCR digest on the GitHub release; the hub and relay container suites fail if a pin is missing.
resources.cveResponse: Pinned by digest and re-pinned by hand in a reviewed change (no Dependabot). The workbench image is not yet scanned in CI; the relay and hub final images are scanned by grype in relay-image-scan.
resources.airGap: needs-mirror:the pinned docker.io/library/node digests, Debian package mirrors and an npm registry mirror holding the locked packages
conditions: A site that builds these images without internet must mirror the pinned image digests, Debian packages and an npm registry with the locked packages, or build elsewhere and import the signed image.
The workbench image uses Debian's OpenSSL, which is not a validated cryptographic module: it is not for Protected B until Phase 46 moves it to UBI 9 in FIPS mode (hosting design #163, section 10).
The workbench image has no sign-in of its own: it runs only behind Theia Cloud's sign-in (Phase 47) or locally on 127.0.0.1 (the entrypoint refuses to start otherwise).
The workbench image is not yet signed or scanned in CI; signing with your organization's key and an SBOM are Phase 46 items.

resources.purpose: Final base image of the relay and hub: Node 26 as a non-root user, with no shell or package manager.
resources.licence: Apache-2.0 (distroless); Node.js MIT and Debian packages under their own licences
resources.evidence: Relay image SBOM (syft) and vulnerability scan (grype) from the relay-image-scan CI job, carried in the evidence bundle.
resources.cveResponse: grype scans the built relay image in the relay-image-scan CI job and fails it on a high fixed vulnerability (a reporting job, not a required check); the digest is re-pinned by hand when Google publishes a fixed image.
resources.airGap: needs-mirror:the pinned gcr.io/distroless/nodejs26-debian13 digest in a local registry
conditions: Air-gapped and on-premise sites must mirror this exact digest into a local registry (gcr.io is a commercial-cloud registry).

The hub's TLS and the relay's token signing run on the Node.js OpenSSL in this image, which is not a FIPS 140 validated module (gap X8): a Protected B deployment needs its authorizing official to accept the comparable-strength basis, or a validated provider.
Act on the relay-image-scan result before each release; it does not block a merge.

resources.purpose: Optional Signal sidecar for the relay (Compose profile "signal", off by default); it relays messages through the Signal service.
resources.licence: MIT (signal-cli-rest-api); bundles signal-cli (GPL-3.0) and libsignal (AGPL-3.0), run as a separate unmodified container
resources.evidence: none
resources.cveResponse: Third-party single-maintainer image pinned by digest; not scanned in CI. signal-cli stops working about three months after release, so the pin lapses about 2026-12-10 (owner decision 2026-11-18: left to lapse until Phase 82).
conditions: Off by default; do not start the "signal" profile until Phase 82 re-pins it to a current release and re-reviews this entry.

It sends messages through the Signal service on the public internet (a commercial service outside your organization): use it only where your organization's policy allows, and never for Protected B, Controlled Goods or ITAR information.
It cannot work at an air-gapped site.
Its cryptography (the Signal protocol in signal-cli) is not a FIPS 140 validated module.
Add it to the image vulnerability scan before it is first used.
